p: Damascus: The chief city of Syria.
Aroer are forsaken: It was a country of Syria by the river Arnon.
Ephraim: It seems that the prophet would comfort the Church in declaring the destruction of these two kings of Syria and Israel, when as they had conspired the overthrow of Judah.
glory of the children of Israel: The ten tribes gloried in their multitude and alliance with other nations: therefore he says that they will be brought down and the Syrians also.
Jacob shall be diminished: Meaning, of the ten tribes who boasted themselves of their nobility, prosperity, strength and multitude.
the grain: As the abundance of corn does not fear the harvest men that would cut it down: no more will the multitude of Israel make the enemies shrink, whom God will appoint to destroy them.
Rephaim: A valley which was plentiful and fertile.
be left in it: Because God would have his covenant stable, he promises to reserve some of this people, and to bring them to repentance.
Maker: He shows that God's corrections always bring fruit, and cause his to turn from their sins and to humble themselves to him.

they left because of the children: As the Canaanites left their cities when God placed the Israelites there, so the cities of Israel will not be able to defend their inhabitants any more than bushes, when God will send the enemy to plague them.
slips: Which are excellent and brought out of other countries.
of grief and of desperate sorrow: As the Lord threatens the wicked in his law, Le 26:16.
Woe to the multitude of many: The prophet laments, considering the horrible plague that was prepared against Israel by the Assyrians, who were infinite in number, and gathered from many nations.
rebuke them: He adds this for the consolation of the faithful who were in Israel.
trouble: He compares the Assyrians to a tempest which rises overnight and in the morning is gone.
